## Important caveats before the numbers

**1. The standard cost-efficiency metric (CASM) cannot be computed from this filing set.** Cost per available seat mile requires ASM capacity data, which is not present in the excerpts available — only dollar-denominated revenue and expense lines are. Everything below is therefore a **revenue-normalized** cost measure (cost as a % of revenue), not a unit-cost measure. These are not the same thing: a carrier with high yields can look "efficient" on a cost/revenue basis while having high unit costs, and vice versa.

**2. Alaska's FY2024 is not comparable to its own prior periods or cleanly to peers.** "On September 18, 2024, Alaska Air Group completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings... The results of Hawaiian are included in the consolidated financial statements beginning September 18, 2024. For the period from the acquisition date to December 31, 2024, revenue and net loss from Hawaiian recognized in the Company's consolidated results of operations was $869 million and $113 million" [alaska_10k_note_acquisition.txt]. Alaska's FY2024 blends ~3.5 months of a loss-making acquiree with a full year of legacy Alaska, plus merger costs.

**3. Business models differ structurally.** Southwest is an all-domestic, single-fleet, point-to-point carrier; Delta, United and American are global network carriers with large long-haul, cargo, loyalty and (for Delta) refinery operations. Cost ratios across these models are not apples-to-apples.

## The data (FY2024, calendar year ended Dec 31, 2024)

| | Revenue | Op. income | Implied opex | Opex/Rev | Op. margin | Labor/Rev | Fuel/Rev |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $61,643M | $5,995M | $55,648M | **90.3%** | **9.7%** | 26.2% | 17.1% |
| United | $57,063M | $5,096M | $51,967M | 91.1% | 8.9% | 29.2% | 20.6% |
| American | $54,211M | $2,614M | $51,597M | 95.2% | 4.8% | 29.6% | 21.1% |
| Alaska | $11,735M | $570M | $11,165M | 95.1% | 4.9% | 30.6% | 21.4% |
| Southwest | $27,483M | $321M | $27,162M | 98.8% | 1.2% | 44.5% | 21.1% |

Source figures: Delta $61,643M revenue / $10,566M fuel / $16,161M labor / $5,995M operating income; United $57,063M / $11,756M / $16,678M / $5,096M; Southwest $27,483M / $5,812M / $12,240M / $321M; American $54,211M / $11,418M / $16,021M / $2,614M; Alaska $11,735M / $2,506M / $3,588M / $570M [airlines_costs_fy2024.txt]. Operating expense is derived as revenue minus operating income.

## Interpretation

- **Delta** absorbs the lowest share of revenue in total operating cost (90.3%) and converts the most to operating profit (9.7% margin), with the lowest labor intensity (26.2% of revenue) and by far the lowest fuel burden (17.1% — helped by its refinery segment, which is embedded in these consolidated figures).
- **United** is a close second (91.1% / 8.9%).
- **Southwest** is the clear laggard on this basis: 98.8% of revenue consumed by operating cost and a 44.5% labor-to-revenue ratio, roughly 15 points above the network carriers. Note this reflects both cost pressure and weak unit revenue/aircraft-delivery disruption, not cost inefficiency alone — and Southwest's low-fare model means low revenue per seat, which inflates any cost/revenue ratio even if its unit costs (CASM) are competitive.
- **American and Alaska** are essentially tied in the middle (~95% opex/revenue), though Alaska's figure is distorted by the Hawaiian consolidation.

**Bottom line:** On the only cost measure derivable from these filings — operating cost as a share of revenue — Delta ranks best. This should be read as "best cost-to-revenue conversion," not "lowest unit costs"; on a true CASM basis Southwest has historically been the low-cost operator among these five, and that ranking cannot be tested with the data available here.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — on the only cost metric derivable from these filings, Delta had the lowest operating expense as a share of revenue (90.3%, vs. United 91.1%, Alaska 95.1%, American 95.2%, Southwest 98.8%) and the highest operating margin (9.7%). Caveat: true unit cost (CASM) cannot be computed because ASM capacity data is not in the source excerpts, and Alaska's FY2024 is distorted by the Sept. 18, 2024 Hawaiian acquisition.
